title: CANcestry FMEDA row (v0.1.0)
description: Row contract for hw/fmeda/fmeda-analysis.csv (issue #56, H-09; HW-SF-005, HW-NF-004; ISO 26262-5:2018 Annex B fault classification, Annex C equations C.1..C.8). One row per (component, failure mode). Inputs: the component base failure rate (fit_total, from hw/bom/fit-database.json via fit_id), the failure-mode distribution fraction, whether the mode is safety-related, whether it can violate the safety goal in the absence of a safety mechanism, whether it is a multiple-point-fault candidate otherwise, the safety mechanism and its diagnostic coverage against single-point faults (dc_spf) and against latent faults (dc_latent). Derived columns (fit_mode, fit_safe, fit_spf_rf, fit_mpf_detected, fit_mpf_latent, classification) are carried for readability and are recomputed by tools/fmeda-calculator.py, which fails closed on any drift. Classification algebra (Annex B/C): not safety related -> excluded; violates_sg=N and mpf_relevant=N -> S (safe); violates_sg=N and mpf_relevant=Y -> MPF with latent share (1 - dc_latent); violates_sg=Y without SM -> SPF; violates_sg=Y with SM -> RF = fit_mode x (1 - dc_spf), the covered part fit_mode x dc_spf becomes MPF with latent share (1 - dc_latent).

fit_total.description: Component base failure rate in FIT (must equal the fit-database entry).

fmd_fraction.description: Failure-mode distribution fraction; the fractions of one part_id sum to exactly 1.

fmd_basis.description: Provenance of the fraction: vendor FMEDA/FMD data, a standard's table, or a documented analyst assumption (T0 placeholder).

violates_sg.description: Can this failure mode violate the safety goal on its own, in the absence of any safety mechanism?

mpf_relevant.description: For violates_sg=N: can the mode contribute to a multiple-point failure (e.g. a fault of a safety mechanism or of the retention energy store)?

sm_spf.description: Safety mechanism preventing the mode from violating the safety goal ('-' when none).

sm_latent.description: Mechanism by which the (covered or MPF) fault is detected or perceived before a second fault ('-' when none).
